clue.text: Season of the old sailor

definitions.meaning: to season food is to add flavouring such as the white crystals from the sea
a veteran seaman

explanation.surface: A question about which time of year belongs to a veteran mariner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the condiment used to flavour food, and the slang term for a seasoned seaman.

clue.text: Flog the party-line

definitions.meaning: to flog is to beat with a lash
in Parliament the written notice telling members how to vote carries this name

explanation.surface: An order to beat the agreed position of a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash used for beating, and the parliamentary instruction that enforces party discipline in votes.

clue.text: Melancholy little boy

definitions.meaning: feeling down, depressed
Little Boy ... of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A small child is feeling sad.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word means sad, and the nursery-rhyme Little Boy who came to blow his horn bears that name.

clue.text: Covetousness is a wicked habit when it ensnares a king

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap, so the wicked habit holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a vice is a wicked or immoral habit
taken as written
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A moral observation that greed is a sin when it traps a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensnares' puts A and R inside VICE to make VARICE, after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed for wealth and possessions is the same thing as wanting what others have.

clue.text: You can tell the tiresome contortionist what to do!

definitions.text: You can tell the tiresome contortionist what to do!

parts.words: You can tell the tiresome contortionist what to do!
parts.note: a rude British dismissal telling someone to go away, read literally as an instruction to a performer who ties himself in knots

explanation.surface: A joke about brushing off a tedious performer by suggesting a fitting act.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a British slang brush-off meaning 'go away'; for a contortionist it is also a literal job description.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang dismissal is what you say to an irritating person, and twisting into knots is what a contortionist does.

clue.text: Give Master Twist a thorough wash! That takes the biscuit

parts.note: a bath gives a full wash of the body
Oliver Twist, the boy in Dickens's novel, addressed as Master

explanation.surface: Telling someone to scrub the Dickens orphan clean, followed by an exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That takes the biscuit' is an idiom for something outrageous, but here the biscuit is the definition: a BATH OLIVER is a plain English cracker.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bath Oliver is a hard, dry English cracker invented in the spa city of Bath.

clue.text: Theoretical solution for reducing a beer-gut?

definitions.text: Theoretical solution for reducing a beer-gut?

parts.words: Theoretical solution for reducing a beer-gut?
parts.note: the underlying reasoning behind something, split as a plan to limit how much beer a drinker has

explanation.surface: A dieter's idea of how to lose the paunch from drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word into two: cutting back your pint (RATION ALE) is the obvious cure for a beer belly, while the whole word means the reasoning behind a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The underlying reasoning or justification behind a course of action is its theoretical basis.

clue.text: Bearing North-East over to the

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Bearing North-East over to the (4)' looks cut short: EN (North-East turned over) is clear, but nothing in the held words gives MI, and no scan or search supplies the missing word.

clue.text: It sheds some illumination on what secondary job-holders do

definitions.meaning: the gentle light reflected from the moon at night
people who work a second job on the side are said to do this

explanation.surface: Something that gives light on the habits of people with second jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The night-time glow from the lunar surface, and the verb for holding an extra job, often undeclared.

clue.text: Ordered to respect such classified information

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to treat a body of restricted intelligence with respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a command but is the anagram signal on TO RESPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Information marked at the highest security grade is classified material.

clue.text: Senior, but not one who has been given a knighthood

definitions.text: one who has been given a knighthood

indicators.note: but not signals that the letters of the word one are taken away from the word senior

explanation.surface: Describing an elderly man who never received an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes O, N and E from SENIOR, leaving S, I, R in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is addressed by this title before his first name.

clue.text: Classic acorn producers

definitions.meaning: one of the five Classic English flat horse races, run at Epsom
trees whose fruit is the acorn

explanation.surface: A description of fine old trees bearing nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Classics are Britain's five great flat races for three-year-olds; the Oaks is the one for fillies at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: The trees whose nuts are acorns share their name with an Epsom horse race.

clue.text: Where to drink some measure of gin neat

indicators.note: only a portion of the words gin neat is taken, a measure poured from them

explanation.surface: Advice on where to go for a shot of undiluted gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some measure of' takes the run of letters inside GIN NEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or tavern is a place to buy a drink.

clue.text: Before 210 Italian isle produced work of note

indicators.note: Before places the island ahead of the number in the answer

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
read digit by digit: 2 as CC (two hundred), 1 as I, 0 as O

explanation.surface: Some event preceding ten past two on an Italian island led to a composition.
explanation.walkthrough: The number is read in Roman fashion digit by digit: CC, I, and O for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a lively, free-form piece of music, so it is a musical composition.

clue.text: Police-chief is full of venom

definitions.note: describes the snake rather than naming it

parts.note: a copper is British slang for a police officer
the head is the chief person

explanation.surface: A poisonous remark about the head of the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the creature: a venomous American pit viper with a coppery head.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American pit viper delivers a poisonous bite.

clue.text: They've got hosts of locations for airborne soldiers

parts.note: paras are paratroopers
sites are places

explanation.surface: Someone has many drop zones for paratroopers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosts' looks like 'lots', but it is the definition: organisms that live off a host.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisms that live on or in another creature need a host to feed from.

clue.text: Letters of pantheist got edited some time ago

indicators.note: edited means the letters have been revised into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A philosopher's writings were revised long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got edited' rearranges the letters of PANTHEIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happened long ago belongs to former times.

clue.text: Kitty somersaults in a circle

indicators.note: a somersault turns the word head over heels, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of shared money

explanation.surface: A cat tumbles round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' is not a cat but a shared fund, POOL; 'somersaults' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed curve that comes back on itself is a ring or circle.

clue.text: Drinks lacking body

definitions.meaning: strong distilled liquors such as whisky and gin
ghosts are disembodied beings

explanation.surface: A complaint about thin, watery beverages.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard liquor shares its name with incorporeal beings such as ghosts.

clue.text: Can anything in New York be indecent?

indicators.note: in places the word for anything inside the abbreviation

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: Asking whether anything in the big city could be risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: AUGHT is archaic for 'anything', as in 'for aught I know'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucy or risqué behaviour is mildly improper.

clue.text: In dispute about a paper-handkerchief

parts.note: a tissue is a disposable paper hanky

explanation.surface: An argument over a paper hanky.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter being argued over is under discussion, the point in question.

clue.text: Critically examines those who attend to creature comforts

definitions.meaning: to vet is to check carefully

definitions.text: those who attend to creature comforts
definitions.meaning: animal doctors look after the wellbeing of creatures

explanation.surface: Inspecting people who look after life's little luxuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creature comforts' usually means small luxuries; here it is literally the comfort of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Screening someone thoroughly, and the animal doctors who treat pets and livestock.

clue.text: Asked earnestly to enter date afresh

indicators.note: afresh means the letters are set down anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone was begged to type in a date again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afresh' rearranges ENTER DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or plead with someone is to ask earnestly.

clue.text: Endless sagas are written about him in the Muslim world

indicators.note: without its ends the word sagas loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Long epics are composed about a figure in Islamic lands.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a commander or chief in the Ottoman Empire and some Muslim countries.
explanation.definitionFit: This title is given to a military commander or official in Turkey and other Muslim lands.

clue.text: One the Military Police see as a mischief-maker

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is the abbreviation for Military Police

explanation.surface: Someone regarded as a troublemaker by the army police.
explanation.definitionFit: A small devilish sprite, or a naughty child, causes trouble.

clue.text: Talk to Tom in French

definitions.meaning: to chatter informally
a tom is a male cat, and the French word for cat

explanation.surface: Speak to a man named Tom in the French language.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is not a man but a tomcat; the French for cat gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal conversation, and the French word for a cat.

clue.text: The policy which gives confidence

definitions.meaning: life cover is sold as this kind of insurance policy in Britain
a feeling of self-confidence and certainty

explanation.surface: An insurance product that reassures its holder.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain life cover is traditionally called life assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of insurance contract, and the self-confidence of someone sure of themselves.

clue.text: Rugby players have an empty hour in Germany

definitions.note: points to a region of Germany rather than naming it

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Rugby players have a free hour while touring Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the Ruhr is an industrial region in western Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr valley is Germany's industrial heartland.

clue.text: Not a single articulate nun

indicators.note: articulate here means spoken, so the word nun is said out loud

parts.note: taken as the word itself, said aloud

explanation.surface: An eloquent sister, the only one of her kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulate' looks like an adjective praising the nun but means 'spoken'.
explanation.definitionFit: Not even one means zero of something.

clue.text: Therefore it's the Cockney woman's turn

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H of her, giving 'er
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Saying it is now the London woman's turn to play.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent that drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word is used in English to mean consequently.

clue.text: They're a drag for jobbing schoolboys

definitions.meaning: cigarettes, which one takes a drag on
at English public schools junior boys who did chores for seniors

explanation.surface: Complaining that boys sent on errands are tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang these are cigarettes; at old English boarding schools they were younger boys who ran errands for older pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for cigarettes, and the junior pupils who served seniors at English boarding schools.

clue.text: To ask for money, then quit, is very dicey

parts.note: to touch someone is British slang for asking them for a loan
and can mean and then, so it stands for next
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Borrowing cash and then leaving is a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'touch' someone for money is British slang for cadging a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome that is uncertain until the last moment is risky.
